title: Any plugins to extract save files from web deployment

posts.author: TinoXelav
posts.body:
Is there a plugin or script I can refer to to extract a save file from an Rpg Maker MZ game from the Web.
I thought of deploying an RPG Maker MZ game and release on the web / html. I also want the players to download a copy of their save file after they save their files on the web. So if the players are playing the game on a different device they can upload their save file and continue their progress without starting over because they play on a different device.

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Old thread might help a little:
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/inde...ing-saves-from-desktop-to-web-version.125176/
I'm unaware of an existing plugin that does specifically what you're asking, but there should be one. You would need to program access options (some login like oauth) and configure a repository per user. I can think of pretty quick ways to do it in Google Play, Steam, or Windows Store, but for a web game I'm at a loss. I am unfamiliar with the Itch.io API, but this is the
reference
. Usually save files are in localstorage cache, so it would be a pretty large tangent for this small feature. For an RPG, it could be worth it.
This makes me think if I had users between multiple platforms, how would I manage the game save files regardless of device? Difficult question.

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
There is the
AltSaveLocation plugin
. You could massage that a bit. It would work in many instances, but not all instances such as kids using library computers or kids using phones/tablets without sufficient permissions. Thinking about where browsers save files and then standardize it can be tricky. You could make the default the download folder. But then you would need to modify the plugin to load from the selected folder.

posts.author: utunnels
caethyril
posts.body:
Freedom said:
Thinking about where browsers save files and then standardize it can be tricky.
Click to expand...
The plugin you linked states it only works for NWJS, because for security reasons browsers do not have standard access to the user's file system. Hence the download/upload idea.
utunnels said:
So if you are lazy you can write a function to extract the whole local storage in a string.
Click to expand...
I'm not sure that's a good idea. There's no guarantee the site's local storage would be dedicated to the game, so you risk deleting/overwriting unrelated values.
I would instead recommend using MZ's existing save/load methods, e.g.
JavaScript:
const id  = 1;                             // Save file ID.
const key = DataManager.makeSaveName(id);  // Storage key.
// Get save data (for export).
const data = StorageManager.loadZip(key);
// Write save data (for import).
StorageManager.saveZip(key, data);
(Copy+paste should work A-OK, assuming there's no practical character limit in place. Manually copying to/from a new .txt file is hardly any less convenient than automatically saving to file.)
I don't think restarting the game would correct missing or mismatched global info, though. So after importing the actual data, it may be necessary to follow up by calling
DataManager.loadGame
and
.saveGame
for each imported save file, since global info entries are generated from the game data at the time of saving.

posts.author: TinoXelav
posts.body:
utunnels said:
RMMZ seems to store save files in local storage of the browser.
View attachment 326679
So if you are lazy you can write a function to extract the whole local storage in a string.
var x = JSON.stringify(localStorage);
prompt('COPY ME!!!!!!!', x);
If you want the user to upload their save:
var x = prompt('PASTE YOUR SAVE HERE:');
localStorage.clear();
Object.assign(localStorage, JSON.parse(x));
However there should be more checks if you want to validate the string the user provides. And make sure to restart the game after that.

You are right. I didn't read the code before so I checked it again.
The screenshot I posted was from a MV game on itch.io. You can see all the save keys use the same pattern: RPG + filename.
So it will be a problem if you play other MV games on the same website.
MZ fixed the problem by providing a game id. So in theory you can check the game id string in those local storage keys.
